page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs spread across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is paired with 15.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, requiring external persistent disks for storage needs.

In synthetic compute benchmarks, the architecture shows moderate throughput relative to modern alternatives. The instance produced a Geekbench single-core score of 927.0 and a multi-core score of 2044.0, while Stress-ng benchmarks registered 1107.78 for single-core and 2904.55 for multi-core. In memory operations, cached 16 KB read bandwidth hit 161.64 GB/sec, dropping to 25.29 GB/sec read and 21.61 GB/sec write on larger 256 MB blocks. Compression benchmarks registered 19.01 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip and 13.47 GB/sec for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Application metrics recorded Redis SET throughput at 2.68 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 2.46 GB/sec.

Due to its older Intel Xeon core architecture and lower per-core compute efficiency, the n1-standard-4 demonstrates slower execution times for compute-heavy compilation, ray tracing, or matrix operations. However, the balanced 1:3.75 CPU-to-memory ratio provides predictable dedicated thread scheduling for standard non-bursty tasks. It fits steady low-demand workloads such as legacy enterprise services, lightweight internal business utilities, test environments, background ETL jobs, and modest web serving tiers where advanced vector instructions are not mandatory.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon processor cores clocked at 2.3 GHz. Configured with an x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 15.0 GB of memory, equating to 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a 45 MB L3 cache. It lacks onboard local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, depending on network-attached storage for volume persistence. Performance across synthetic benchmarks reflects its earlier-generation Intel silicon, recording a Geekbench multi-core rating of 2044.0 and PassMark score of 3497.41. Large-block memory throughput reaches 25.29 GB/sec read and 21.61 GB/sec write, with static web throughput measured at 2.46 GB/sec. Given its modest instruction throughput and balanced allocation profile, n1-standard-4 serves best in steady baseline utility workloads, low-concurrency web tiers, lightweight backend microservices, and general testing pipelines that do not demand cutting-edge per-core processing rates.
